Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the data, I need to compare:
1. Model forecasts (30-day ahead)
2. True outcomes (30 days)

Let me examine each example to find patterns in errors.

## Example 1: Date=2025-07-30

History price: Starts around 70.42-71.67 range, ending at 73.08
Model forecast at day 1: 72.98
True outcome at day 1: 72.86
Difference: -0.12

Model forecast at day 15: 71.02
True outcome at day 15: 71.29
Difference: +0.27 (model was too low)

Model forecast at day 30: 74.23
True outcome at day 30: 76.90
Difference: +2.67 (model significantly too low at horizon)

Let me look at the pattern more carefully:

Looking at the first 5 days of forecasts vs outcomes:
Day 1: Model 72.98 vs True 72.86 (off by -0.12)
Day 2: Model 72.80 vs True 72.66 (off by -0.14)
Day 3: Model 71.36 vs True 71.04 (off by -0.32)
Day 4: Model 71.29 vs True 70.85 (off by -0.44)
Day 5: Model 71.92 vs True 71.59 (off by -0.33)

The model appears to be under-predicting, especially as we get further out. The gap increases from about 0.1-0.3 cents in the near term to 2.67 cents at day 30.
